records.text: 2.1.1. If an effect includes “you may,” you may choose not to resolve that part of the effect.

records.text: 2.3. Resolve card effects in the order they appear on the card.

records.title: If you can’t resolve the entirety of an effect, resolve as much of it as you possibly can.
records.text: 2.4. If you can’t resolve the entirety of an effect, resolve as much of it as you possibly can.

records.text: 2.8. When cards or effects specify “up to,” you can choose none or 0 (unless there’s a specified minimum).

records.title: To play a Program, reveal the card to your Rival, pay its cost, resolve its effect(s), and immediately move it to you…
records.text: 4.14. To play a Program, reveal the card to your Rival, pay its cost, resolve its effect(s), and immediately move it to your trash.

records.title: When you reveal a played Program, place it on the table to allow your Rival to read and understand its effects before…
records.text: 4.14.1. When you reveal a played Program, place it on the table to allow your Rival to read and understand its effects before you resolve it.

records.title: After you pay a Program’s cost, the card is considered outside of your hand, field, trash, or any other game area unt…
records.text: 4.14.2. After you pay a Program’s cost, the card is considered outside of your hand, field, trash, or any other game area until you finish resolving its effects (though it’s not considered “Removed from Play”). After you resolve the program, it enters your trash.

records.title: A game area may be “public” or “hidden.”
records.text: 5.3. A game area may be “public” or “hidden.”

records.title: If a game area is public, these rules apply.
records.text: 5.3.1. If a game area is public, these rules apply.

records.title: Face-up cards in a public area are known to all players.
records.text: 5.3.1.1. Face-up cards in a public area are known to all players. You can look at information on all face-up cards at any time.

records.title: Face-down cards in a public area aren’t publicly known.
records.text: 5.3.1.2. Face-down cards in a public area aren’t publicly known. You can’t look at them unless directed by an effect.

records.title: If a game area is hidden, these rules apply.
records.text: 5.3.2. If a game area is hidden, these rules apply.

records.title: Cards in a hidden area aren’t publicly known.
records.text: 5.3.2.1. Cards in a hidden area aren’t publicly known. You can’t look at them unless directed by an effect.

records.title: If a card enters a hidden area, ignore any information on the card and remove any existing modifiers attached to it.
records.text: 5.3.2.2. If a card enters a hidden area, ignore any information on the card and remove any existing modifiers attached to it.

records.title: If an effect requires you to reveal and move a card from a hidden area, you must reveal the card before moving it to…
records.text: 5.3.2.3. If an effect requires you to reveal and move a card from a hidden area, you must reveal the card before moving it to another area.

records.title: When you search for a card in a hidden area, you do not have to reveal any information about your findings if you fai…
records.text: 5.3.2.4. When you search for a card in a hidden area, you do not have to reveal any information about your findings if you fail to find a valid target. See Search.

records.title: If an effect requires a player to choose from a hidden area using information that is not public, that player may cho…
records.text: 5.3.2.4.1. If an effect requires a player to choose from a hidden area using information that is not public, that player may choose to fail to find a target.

records.title: If an effect requires you to choose from a hidden area without requiring a qualifying card information, you must choo…
records.text: 5.3.2.5. If an effect requires you to choose from a hidden area without requiring a qualifying card information, you must choose a legal target. You are not required to reveal it.

records.title: If an effect instructs you to look at or search cards in a hidden area and does not say what to do with cards not cho…
records.text: 5.3.2.6. If an effect instructs you to look at or search cards in a hidden area and does not say what to do with cards not chosen, return those cards to their original area in their original order and state.

records.title: 1 polyhedral die represents 1 Gig.
records.text: 6.1. 1 polyhedral die represents 1 Gig. Gigs are also referred to as “Gig dice” (and variations thereof).

records.title: Gig dice are represented by d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, d20.
records.text: 6.1.1. Gig dice are represented by d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, d20. These designations refer both to the number of sides on a die and the highest value a die can reach.

records.title: You control the Gigs in your Gig area.
records.text: 6.1.2. You control the Gigs in your Gig area. They are considered “friendly Gigs”.

records.title: You don’t control the Gig dice in your fixer area.
records.text: 6.1.3. You don’t control the Gig dice in your fixer area. They are not considered friendly Gigs.

records.title: You can’t target Gig dice in the fixer area to fulfill or resolve effects.
records.text: 6.1.4. You can’t target Gig dice in the fixer area to fulfill or resolve effects.

records.title: A Gig’s value is the number on its current top face.
records.text: 6.3. A Gig’s value is the number on its current top face.

records.title: A min Gig is any Gig die at its lowest possible value.
records.text: 6.3.1. A min Gig is any Gig die at its lowest possible value.

records.title: A max Gig is any Gig die at its highest possible value.
records.text:
6.3.2. A max Gig is any Gig die at its highest possible value.

> **EXAMPLE:** A d4 has four sides with possible values of 1, 2, 3, and 4. If its current value is 4, then it’s a max Gig.

records.title: The highest value on a die is always equal to its number of sides, and the lowest value on a die is always 1.
records.text:
6.3.3. The highest value on a die is always equal to its number of sides, and the lowest value on a die is always 1. This is true even if the specific die represents the number differently.

> **EXAMPLE:** If the faces of your d10 are labelled 0-9, the 0 represents “10” and is considered the highest value, while the 1 is considered the lowest value.

records.title: Adjust a Gig by changing its value.
records.text: 6.4. Adjust a Gig by changing its value.

records.title: “Increase” a Gig by adjusting to a higher number.
records.text: 6.4.1. “Increase” a Gig by adjusting to a higher number.

records.title: “Decrease” a Gig by adjusting to a lower number.
records.text: 6.4.2. “Decrease” a Gig by adjusting to a lower number.

records.title: “Set” a Gig by adjusting it to a specific value.
records.text: 6.4.3. “Set” a Gig by adjusting it to a specific value.

records.title: You cannot adjust a Gig to a value that isn’t on its face.
records.text: 6.4.4. You cannot adjust a Gig to a value that isn’t on its face. (i.e. set a d6 to 8). If an effect tells you to do so, the effect fails.

records.title: A Gig’s value cannot be adjusted to the value it already has.
records.text:
6.4.5. A Gig’s value cannot be adjusted to the value it already has. If an effect tells you to do so, the effect fails.

> **EXAMPLE:** If a Gig is at a min value, it cannot be changed to its min value by an effect. You may choose it for an effect that could adjust it to a min, but nothing would happen.

records.title: Play a Card
records.text:
8.13. ### Play a Card

As an action during your Main phase, you may play a card from your hand. See Play.

records.title: Activate an Effect
records.text:
8.14. ### Activate an Effect

As an action during your Main phase, you may activate any activated effects on friendly Units or Legends. They may be used during the open state of the main phase. For the full rules on activating effects, see EFFECTS > Activated Effects.

records.title: You cannot activate [Spend Icon] effects on Lagging Units.
records.text: 8.14.1. You cannot activate [Spend Icon] effects on Lagging Units. See Lag.

records.title: To “resolve” an effect, follow the instructions of that effect in the order they appear.
records.text: 10.2. To “resolve” an effect, follow the instructions of that effect in the order they appear.

records.title: Always resolve as much of an effect as possible.
records.text: 10.2.1. Always resolve as much of an effect as possible. See GOLDEN RULES > Resolve as Much as Possible.

records.title: If an effect instructs both players to act at the same time, the turn player performs their actions first, followed b…
records.text: 10.2.2. If an effect instructs both players to act at the same time, the turn player performs their actions first, followed by their Rival.

records.title: Once an effect starts resolving, you cannot play cards, activate effects, or resolve other pending effects until the…
records.text: 10.2.3. Once an effect starts resolving, you cannot play cards, activate effects, or resolve other pending effects until the current effect finishes resolving.

records.title: Effects cannot interrupt the activation or resolution of other effects.
records.text: 10.2.4. Effects cannot interrupt the activation or resolution of other effects. If an effect triggers in the middle of an activation or resolution, it becomes “pending resolution.” See EFFECTS > Pending Resolution.

records.title: After an effect resolves, perform any required rule processing before resolving a new one or taking any actions.
records.text: 10.2.5. After an effect resolves, perform any required rule processing before resolving a new one or taking any actions.

records.title: An effect is “valid” if it can apply according to its text, the game rules, and the current game state.
records.text: 10.5. An effect is “valid” if it can apply according to its text, the game rules, and the current game state.

records.title: An effect is “invalid” if it cannot apply according to its text, the game rules, or the current game state.
records.text: 10.6. An effect is “invalid” if it cannot apply according to its text, the game rules, or the current game state.

records.title: If all of an effect is invalid, ignore that effect.
records.text: 10.6.1. If all of an effect is invalid, ignore that effect.

records.title: If part of an effect is invalid, ignore the invalid part and resolve as much of the remaining effect as possible.
records.text: 10.6.2. If part of an effect is invalid, ignore the invalid part and resolve as much of the remaining effect as possible.

records.title: Even if an effect is invalid, it is still considered an effect on the card.
records.text: 10.6.3. Even if an effect is invalid, it is still considered an effect on the card.

records.title: If an effect requires a target or choice with no legal options, the effect is invalid and the controlling player does…
records.text: 10.7. If an effect requires a target or choice with no legal options, the effect is invalid and the controlling player does not make a choice.

records.title: If an activated effect requires a target or choice as part of activation cost but no legal target or choice exists, t…
records.text: 10.8. If an activated effect requires a target or choice as part of activation cost but no legal target or choice exists, the effect is invalid and you cannot activate it.

records.title: If an activated effect has additional activation conditions that are invalid, you cannot activate the effect.
records.text: 10.9. If an activated effect has additional activation conditions that are invalid, you cannot activate the effect.

records.title: If an effect becomes invalid after it activates or becomes pending, still resolve as much of the effect as possible.
records.text: 10.10. If an effect becomes invalid after it activates or becomes pending, still resolve as much of the effect as possible.

records.title: If resolving a pending effect requires information about a game piece that is no longer valid, use the information fr…
records.text: 10.10.1. If resolving a pending effect requires information about a game piece that is no longer valid, use the information from when the piece was last valid.

records.title: You may activate “activated effects” as an action during your Main Phase.
records.text: 10.18. You may activate “activated effects” as an action during your Main Phase. See Activate an Effect.

records.title: You cannot activate an activated effect while resolving another action or effect, nor while any effects are pending r…
records.text: 10.18.1. You cannot activate an activated effect while resolving another action or effect, nor while any effects are pending resolution.

records.title: When an activated effect has a colon, the bolded text preceding the colon is the activation cost, and the text follow…
records.text:
10.19. When an activated effect has a colon, the bolded text preceding the colon is the activation cost, and the text following the colon is the effect that resolves after you pay the activation cost. See Cost.

> **EXAMPLE:** A friendly Unit’s effect text reads "[Spend Icon] Swap a friendly Gig with a rival Gig.” This is an activated effect. During your Main Phase, you may spend the Unit as an activation cost; if you do, you gain the effect “Swap a friendly Gig with a rival Gig.”

records.title: Choices and costs before the colon are made or paid while activating the effect.
records.text: 10.19.1. Choices and costs before the colon are made or paid while activating the effect. Choices after the colon are made while resolving the effect.

records.title: You must pay all activation costs for an effect.
records.text: 10.19.2. You must pay all activation costs for an effect. If you can’t pay all required costs, you cannot activate the effect.

records.title: If an effect has multiple activation costs, pay them in the order that they appear.
records.text: 10.19.3. If an effect has multiple activation costs, pay them in the order that they appear.

records.title: Activate an activated effect by completing these steps in order.
records.text: 10.20. Activate an activated effect by completing these steps in order.

records.title: Choose a valid friendly effect to activate.
records.text: 10.20.1. Choose a valid friendly effect to activate. See EFFECTS > Valid & Invalid Effects.

records.title: If the activated effect is on a card in a hidden area (like your hand), reveal it.
records.text: 10.20.2. If the activated effect is on a card in a hidden area (like your hand), reveal it.

records.title: If the effect requires a choice or valid target, choose them.
records.text: 10.20.3. If the effect requires a choice or valid target, choose them.

records.title: Pay all activation costs in the order they appear.
records.text: 10.20.4. Pay all activation costs in the order they appear. When you do, any effects triggered by the activation become pending.

records.title: Communicate the effect and any choices/targets to your Rival.
records.text: 10.20.5. Communicate the effect and any choices/targets to your Rival.

records.title: Resolve the effect.
records.text: 10.20.6. Resolve the effect. When you do, any effects triggered by the resolution become pending.

records.title: Resolve any pending effects.
records.text: 10.20.7. Resolve any pending effects.

records.title: Once an activated effect is activated, it resolves even if its source leaves the area it was in.
records.text: 10.21. Once an activated effect is activated, it resolves even if its source leaves the area it was in.

records.title: If an effect instructs a player to choose, select, or otherwise make a choice, that choice is made when the effect in…
records.text: 10.31. If an effect instructs a player to choose, select, or otherwise make a choice, that choice is made when the effect instructs the player to make that choice.

records.title: If an effect requires a choice and no legal choice can be made, that choice is not made.
records.text: 10.31.1. If an effect requires a choice and no legal choice can be made, that choice is not made.

records.title: If an effect requires you to choose a specific number of targets, you must choose that number of targets.
records.text: 10.31.2. If an effect requires you to choose a specific number of targets, you must choose that number of targets. If you can’t, choose as many valid targets as possible up to that number instead.

records.title: If an effect requires a player to choose a number, that player must choose a non-negative whole number.
records.text: 10.31.3. If an effect requires a player to choose a number, that player must choose a non-negative whole number.

records.title: Cost
A “cost” details what you must pay to play a card, activate an effect, or perform a game action.
records.text: 11.1.1. A “cost” details what you must pay to play a card, activate an effect, or perform a game action. See Pay.

records.title: To play a card, you must pay its cost value in the top left corner of the card.
records.text: 11.1.1.1. To play a card, you must pay its cost value in the top left corner of the card. See Cost Value.

records.title: An activation cost is a cost that must be paid to activate an effect.
records.text: 11.1.1.2. An activation cost is a cost that must be paid to activate an effect. See EFFECTS > Activated Effects.

records.title: A cost must be paid in full; if you cannot pay all required costs, you cannot play the card, activate the effect, nor…
records.text: 11.1.2. A cost must be paid in full; if you cannot pay all required costs, you cannot play the card, activate the effect, nor perform the game action associated with it

records.title: If a cost is replaced by another cost, pay the replacement cost instead of the original cost.
records.text: 11.1.2.1. If a cost is replaced by another cost, pay the replacement cost instead of the original cost. The replacement cost must be paid in full.

records.title: [Star] Street Cred
records.text: 11.2. ### [Star] Street Cred

records.title: Your “Street Cred” is the sum of all Gig dice values in the friendly Gig area.
records.text: 11.2.1. Your “Street Cred” is the sum of all Gig dice values in the friendly Gig area.

records.title: The [Star] symbol is shorthand for Street Cred.
records.text: 11.2.2. The [Star] symbol is shorthand for Street Cred.

records.title: When you have no Gigs in your Gig area you have Null ( - ) Street Cred.
records.text: 11.2.3. When you have no Gigs in your Gig area you have Null ( - ) Street Cred. Null does not count as having 0.

records.title: Lag
Lag is a condition applied to Units when they enter the field.
records.text: 11.3.1. Lag is a condition applied to Units when they enter the field. Units with Lag are also called “lagging.”

records.title: Lagging Units can’t attack.
records.text: 11.3.1.1. Lagging Units can’t attack.

records.title: Lagging Units can’t activate [Spend Icon] effects.
records.text: 11.3.1.2. Lagging Units can’t activate [Spend Icon] effects.

records.title: At the end of each turn, all Units lose the “Lag” condition.
records.text: 11.3.2. At the end of each turn, all Units lose the “Lag” condition.

records.title: Play
To play a card, reveal it, pay its cost, and then follow the rules for playing that specific card type detailed in {C…
records.text: 11.4.1. To play a card, reveal it, pay its cost, and then follow the rules for playing that specific card type detailed in CARD TYPES.

records.title: If you can’t pay for or follow the rules for playing the card, you cannot play it.
records.text: 11.4.1.1. If you can’t pay for or follow the rules for playing the card, you cannot play it. It’s considered “invalid” to play.

records.title: If you play or attempt to play an invalid card, undo the play attempt and return the game to the previous legal game…
records.text: 11.4.1.2. If you play or attempt to play an invalid card, undo the play attempt and return the game to the previous legal game state as much as possible.

records.title: You can only play cards from your hand unless an effect instructs otherwise.
records.text: 11.4.2. You can only play cards from your hand unless an effect instructs otherwise.

records.title: Effects that allow a player to play a card follows the normal rules for playing that card unless the effect instructs…
records.text: 11.4.3. Effects that allow a player to play a card follows the normal rules for playing that card unless the effect instructs otherwise.

records.title: Draw
“Draw” is a game action in which you move the top card of your deck to your hand.
records.text: 11.5.1. “Draw” is a game action in which you move the top card of your deck to your hand.

records.title: When an effect says “Draw X” (where X is a number), take the draw action X number of times.
records.text: 11.5.2. When an effect says “Draw X” (where X is a number), take the draw action X number of times. Literally, it means “move the top card of your deck to your hand, X individual times.”

records.title: When you “Draw X,” draw each card individually.
records.text: 11.5.2.1. When you “Draw X,” draw each card individually. Do not take multiple cards from the top of your deck at once.

records.title: When you “Draw up to X,” choose the number of cards you will draw, then draw exactly that number of cards.
records.text: 11.5.2.2. When you “Draw up to X,” choose the number of cards you will draw, then draw exactly that number of cards.

records.title: If you attempt to draw more cards than remain in your deck, it counts as drawing from an empty deck.
records.text: 11.5.2.3. If you attempt to draw more cards than remain in your deck, it counts as drawing from an empty deck. See GAME OVERVIEW > Lose Conditions.

records.title: [Spend Icon] (Spend Icon)
records.text: 11.15. ### [Spend Icon] (Spend Icon)

records.title: The [Spend Icon] symbol is shorthand for an activation cost.
records.text:
11.15.1. The [Spend Icon] symbol is shorthand for an activation cost. It means: “Spend this Unit or Legend to activate the following effect.”

> **EXAMPLE:** A friendly Unit has the effect “[Spend Icon] Draw 1.” The [Spend Icon] symbol is an activation trigger. You must specifically spend this Unit as a cost. If you do, you draw a card.

records.title: To activate a [Spend Icon] effect, you must spend the card with the express purpose of paying its activation cost.
records.text: 11.15.2. To activate a [Spend Icon] effect, you must spend the card with the express purpose of paying its activation cost. When you spend a Unit or Legend with this symbol for any other reason, it does not trigger the [Spend Icon] effect.

records.title: After paying the cost to use a [Spend Icon] effect, immediately resolve the effect.
records.text: 11.15.3. After paying the cost to use a [Spend Icon] effect, immediately resolve the effect.

records.title: If a [Spend Icon] effect also has a condition, the condition must be met at the time of activation and resolution.
records.text: 11.15.3.1. If a [Spend Icon] effect also has a condition, the condition must be met at the time of activation and resolution.

records.title: If additional effects conditions are met in the process of using a [Spend Icon:] effect, resolve the [Spend Icon] eff…
records.text: 11.15.3.2. If additional effects conditions are met in the process of using a [Spend Icon:] effect, resolve the [Spend Icon] effect, then resolve any other pending effects.

records.title: “X €$” (where X is a number) denotes Eddies and/or Legends spent to pay a cost.
records.text: 11.16.1. “X €$” (where X is a number) denotes Eddies and/or Legends spent to pay a cost.

records.title: When bolded and preceding a colon, before the effect text, it represents an activation cost (or part of an activation…
records.text:
11.16.1.1. When bolded and preceding a colon, before the effect text, it represents an activation cost (or part of an activation cost) for the effect. It means: “Pay X to activate the following effect.”

> **EXAMPLE:** A friendly Legend has the text “1 €$, [Spend Icon] Give a friendly Unit +1 power this turn for each of its equipped Gear.“ So, to activate this effect, you must spend this Legend and 1 other Eddie or Legend.

records.title: Trigger keywords are a shorthand for specific conditions.
records.text:
11.17. Trigger keywords are a shorthand for specific conditions. When those conditions are met, the effect associated with it automatically enters pending.

> **EXAMPLE:** A friendly Unit has the effect “[ATTACK] Draw 1.” [ATTACK] is a timing trigger. Whenever this Unit attacks, you draw a card.
